items.title: Russia claims overnight strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said overnight strikes targeted Ukrainian energy and transport infrastructure, industrial facilities and a cargo vessel allegedly carrying military supplies. Reports citing local authorities described electricity and heating disruptions in Zaporizhzhia. The claimed military use of the targets and extent of damage have not been independently verified.

items.title: Russian-appointed official outlines possible Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant restart
items.summary: Russian-appointed regional governor Yevgeny Balitsky claimed the nuclear power plant could resume operations within two to three months after hostilities end. He said alternative water sources could provide reactor cooling. The proposed timeline and technical feasibility have not been independently verified.

items.title: Frozen Russian assets in Switzerland reportedly exceed $10 billion
items.summary: Bloomberg reportedly puts the value of Russian assets frozen in Switzerland above $10 billion, reflecting additional asset freezes and an increase in the value of some gold holdings.

items.title: Russia reports arrest over alleged attack on regional official
items.summary: Russia's Federal Security Service announced the detention of a suspect in an alleged attack on an official in Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia region. Russian authorities allege Ukrainian involvement and say the official was unharmed. The allegations have not been independently verified.

items.title: Russia claims 305 Ukrainian drones intercepted overnight
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry reported intercepting 305 Ukrainian drones across Russian regions overnight. The nationwide figure has not been independently verified.

items.title: Boris Johnson advocates sending European troops to Ukraine
items.summary: Former British Prime Minister Boris Johnson reportedly advocated deploying European troops to Ukraine in a Sky News interview, arguing that NATO is stronger than Russia. His remarks do not represent an announced government deployment decision.

items.title: Russian-appointed Donetsk authorities report civilian injuries
items.summary: Russian-appointed authorities in occupied Donetsk region reported civilian injuries from alleged Ukrainian attacks over the preceding day, including incidents involving civilian vehicles. The accounts have not been independently verified.

items.title: Around 100 schools in occupied Luhansk region move to remote learning
items.summary: Russian-appointed education official Yevgeny Miroshnichenko said around 100 schools had moved to remote or hybrid learning, most of them near the front line. He said parental preferences also influenced decisions in some municipalities.

items.title: Medvedev warns against NATO troop deployment to Ukraine
items.summary: Russian Security Council deputy chairman Dmitry Medvedev warned that former British prime minister Boris Johnson's proposal to deploy NATO troops to Ukraine could lead to direct war with Russia. Medvedev also made a violent threat against Johnson in the event of such a conflict.

items.title: Russian Foreign Ministry issues warning over Estonia
items.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry accused Estonia of actions that it said risk provoking an open war with Russia. The available statement did not specify the actions in question or include an Estonian response.

items.title: Polish deputy defence minister warns against severing ties with Russia
items.summary: Deputy Defence Minister Stanisław Wziątek warned in a radio interview that breaking diplomatic relations with Russia could create a risk of war. His remarks followed Poland's summoning of the Russian ambassador over an alleged airspace violation.

items.title: US travel advisory warns against visiting Ukraine
items.summary: Reports citing an updated US State Department advisory say Ukraine remains at Level 4, the highest travel warning, citing the risk of missile and drone attacks throughout the country.

items.title: Russian-appointed Luhansk officials announce additional school generators
items.summary: The Russian-appointed regional education minister said around 600 generators had already been supplied to educational institutions and more than 100 additional units were planned before year-end.

items.title: Russian-appointed Donetsk mayor reports overnight damage
items.summary: The mayor said an alleged Ukrainian drone attack damaged a residential building's roof and destroyed eight vehicles. The account has not been independently verified.

items.title: European Commission proposes additional sanctions on Russia
items.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen outlined proposed restrictions on Russian-insured tankers and the blacklisting of around 70 vessels suspected of transporting Russian oil. Separate reports describe proposed visa restrictions on current and former Russian military personnel and restrictions on Europeans serving on Russian corporate boards.

items.title: Estonia rules out allowing Ukrainian strikes from its territory
items.summary: Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal reportedly said Estonia would not permit Ukraine to use its airspace, territorial waters or land to attack Russian targets. The remarks follow recent tensions between Moscow and Tallinn.

items.title: Naftogaz reports shutdown at Poltava gas facility
items.summary: Ukraine's Naftogaz reportedly said operations at a gas extraction facility in Poltava region had stopped following an overnight strike and resulting fire.

items.title: Russian-appointed authorities report widespread Donetsk power outages
items.summary: The Russian-appointed regional energy ministry said more than 42,000 customers were without electricity across ten districts in occupied Donetsk region, attributing the outages to alleged Ukrainian drone attacks and a power shortage. The account has not been independently verified.

items.title: Murmansk governor arrested in alleged embezzlement case
items.summary: Russian authorities reported the arrest of Governor Andrei Chibis in a case involving alleged theft of more than 39 million rubles in public funds and alleged misappropriation of more than one billion rubles allocated to road reconstruction. The allegations have not been adjudicated.

items.title: French Senate scrutinizes military mission in Ukraine
items.summary: Deputy Defence Minister Alice Rufo was reportedly summoned to a closed Senate hearing over the deployment of French personnel to Ukraine without parliamentary notification. Opposition lawmakers question the legality of the mission, while the Defence Ministry argues that notification requirements do not apply to noncombat missions.

items.title: Kremlin says next Abu Dhabi negotiations remain unscheduled
items.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Moscow remains open to negotiations with Ukraine and contacts with Europe, but no date has been set for the next round of talks in Abu Dhabi. He described existing working-level contacts with EU representatives as largely unproductive.

items.title: Russia allocates additional 20 billion rubles for roads in occupied Ukrainian regions
items.summary: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Marat Khusnullin told the State Duma that the government had approved additional road construction funding last week. He also claimed tax collections in the occupied regions had increased by 11 percent.

items.title: Germany's Merz and AfD clash over Ukraine policy
items.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz accused Russia of escalating tensions beyond Ukraine and pledged a European response. AfD co-leader Tino Chrupalla criticized the allocation of another €11 billion in military aid for Ukraine in 2027, arguing that Germany should prioritize domestic infrastructure and economic needs.

items.title: EU reportedly considering broader restrictions on Russian tourism
items.summary: A report citing an EU Council document says the bloc intends to substantially reduce Russian tourist arrivals. France, which previously opposed such proposals alongside Italy, is reportedly considering changing its position. No final decision was reported.

items.title: EU proposes winter energy truce and Black Sea shipping agreement
items.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen outlined new proposed preconditions for negotiations with Russia, including a winter-long energy truce and an agreement on safe passage for shipping to Ukraine through the Black Sea. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov separately said Moscow wanted clarification of Europe's intended role in negotiations.

items.title: Poland reportedly proposes NATO missile interceptions over Ukraine
items.summary: According to a report citing Bloomberg, Poland suggested that NATO members consider intercepting Russian missiles over Ukraine if they are believed to be heading toward NATO territory. The proposal was reportedly discussed by ambassadors on November 23, but no decision was reached.

items.title: Odesa faces renewed electricity disruptions
items.summary: Ukraine's energy company DTEK reportedly said parts of Odesa were without electricity following another strike on energy infrastructure, with disruptions also affecting critical services.

items.title: Lukashenko raises possibility of removing Russian nuclear-capable missiles
items.summary: Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko reportedly said he would not rule out the withdrawal of Russian nuclear-capable missiles from Belarus if necessary for peace. He also argued that Russia must be included in any European security framework. No withdrawal agreement was announced.

items.title: Russia proposes new import duties on goods from unfriendly countries
items.summary: Russian Deputy Finance Minister Alexey Sazanov said the Finance Ministry had proposed a 15% import duty on delicacy food products from countries Moscow classifies as unfriendly, starting January 1, 2027. The proposal has been submitted to the Economic Development Ministry.

items.title: Polish deputy defence minister says NATO opposes interceptions over Ukraine
items.summary: Polish Deputy Defence Minister Cezary Tomczyk said NATO considers intercepting missiles over Ukrainian territory unacceptable. His remarks follow reports that Warsaw had asked allies to examine the possibility.

items.title: Norway restricts entry for Russian and Belarusian athletes
items.summary: Norway's government announced restrictions on entry for Russian and Belarusian athletes. The available announcement did not specify the full scope of the measures.

items.title: SAPO presents draft policy on corruption plea agreements
items.summary: Ukraine's Specialized Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office presented proposed criteria for plea agreements in high-level corruption cases, including cooperation with investigators, proportionality and compensation for losses. The draft also calls for annual publication of aggregate results, including recovered assets.

items.title: Russia and Brunei announce strategic partnership
items.summary: President Vladimir Putin announced a joint declaration elevating bilateral relations to a strategic partnership. He outlined plans to expand energy cooperation, banking links and settlement in national currencies to reduce exposure to international political and market disruptions.

items.title: Belgian court reportedly freezes €115 million in Google Belgium assets
items.summary: According to a report citing a person familiar with the court decision, a Belgian court ordered a precautionary freeze on €115 million in Google Belgium assets at the request of the Russian Google entity. The reported measure concerns dividends.

items.title: Poland plans no-fly zone along Ukrainian border
items.summary: Polish Deputy Defence Minister Cezary Tomczyk reportedly said Poland plans to establish a no-fly zone along its border with Ukraine by late December or early January. The announcement follows discussions about protecting NATO airspace.

items.title: Russia prepares response to possible seizure of frozen assets
items.summary: Russian Foreign Ministry economic cooperation official Dmitry Birichevsky said Moscow has prepared additional measures in case its frozen assets are confiscated. He did not specify the measures in the available report.

items.title: US-led consortium reportedly prepares bid for Lukoil's overseas assets
items.summary: Reuters reportedly says a consortium led by American businessman Todd Boehly is preparing a deal to acquire Lukoil's foreign assets, with sources expecting an agreement within weeks. No completed transaction was announced.

items.title: Putin dismisses Murmansk governor following arrest
items.summary: President Vladimir Putin terminated Andrei Chibis's tenure as Murmansk governor by decree. Chibis, who was arrested in a case involving alleged embezzlement and bribery, denies guilt according to his lawyer.

items.title: Legal experts question legality of reported Ukrainian strike in Libya
items.summary: A report citing international maritime law experts says the reported Ukrainian attack on a vessel in Benghazi likely violated Libya's neutrality and sovereignty. The experts' assessments are not a court ruling.

items.title: US reportedly approves potential $621.9 million F-16 support package for Ukraine
items.summary: The US State Department reportedly approved a potential package to sustain Ukraine's F-16 fleet, financed by Belgium, Denmark, the Netherlands and Norway through JUMPSTART rather than US funds. The approval does not establish that deliveries have occurred.

items.title: Kushner anticipates major Russia–Ukraine prisoner exchange before year-end
items.summary: US presidential envoy Jared Kushner said a large prisoner exchange between Russia and Ukraine is expected before the end of the year. No numbers or agreed date were provided in the available report.

items.title: Kushner outlines US approach to Ukraine peace negotiations
items.summary: Jared Kushner said Washington would support a settlement that ends hostilities and that the coming weeks would indicate whether its negotiating approach works. He said the US understands Moscow's reluctance to accept a ceasefire without a peace agreement and argued that US security guarantees must serve American interests.

items.title: Russian embassy in Moldova warns of alleged provocation
items.summary: Russia's embassy in Moldova said it had received information about a planned anti-Russian provocation and urged Chisinau to avoid escalation. The embassy's allegation was not independently verified, and the available reports provided no specific details or Moldovan response.

items.title: NATO reportedly hopes US will delay European troop withdrawal decision
items.summary: Bloomberg, citing unnamed sources, reported that NATO expects Washington to postpone a decision on withdrawing some US troops from Europe as the Trump administration focuses on Ukraine peace negotiations. The sources also cited improved relations over allied defence spending. No formal postponement was announced.

items.title: Latvian prime minister criticizes Estonia's Russian border transport decision
items.summary: Latvian Prime Minister Kulbergs reportedly described Estonia's decision to close transport links at the Russian border as a mistake, urging consideration of how traffic could be redirected through neighboring countries.

items.title: Renewed strikes reported in Kyiv
items.summary: Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko reportedly confirmed a strike on a warehouse. Separate accounts alleged damage to energy infrastructure and reported a fire. The full extent of damage has not been independently established.

items.title: Protests reportedly follow prolonged power outages in Dnipro
items.summary: Local social media accounts reportedly described residents blocking streets after prolonged electricity outages. A city council deputy said some districts had experienced outages lasting two to three days, with generators unable to fully meet apartment buildings' electricity and heating needs.

items.title: Putin highlights national-currency trade with Kazakhstan
items.summary: Meeting Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev in Moscow, Vladimir Putin said bilateral trade had exceeded $28 billion and more than 90% of settlements were conducted in national currencies. He also outlined opportunities for cooperation in artificial intelligence and other high-tech industries.

items.title: Fire reported at Kyiv shopping centre following strikes
items.summary: Reports described a fire at Kyiv's Prospect shopping centre following renewed strikes on the Ukrainian capital. The cause and extent of damage have not been independently verified.

items.title: Further strikes reported in Kryvyi Rih and Kharkiv
items.summary: A Russian military correspondent reported a fire following a strike in Kryvyi Rih and further strikes in Kharkiv. The reports have not been independently verified.

items.title: Russian deputy prime minister visits Afghanistan for trade talks
items.summary: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexey Overchuk arrived in Afghanistan leading a Russian delegation. He said the Taliban authorities were interested in purchasing Russian vehicles, energy supplies, food, grain and fertilizers.

items.title: Poland reportedly tests drone integration in mechanized infantry
items.summary: Reports describe Polish military exercises evaluating a pilot project to integrate unmanned systems into a mechanized infantry battalion, reflecting the growing importance of drones and counter-drone capabilities in modern warfare.

items.title: CIS secretary-general says national-currency trade helps offset Western sanctions
items.summary: CIS Secretary-General Sergei Lebedev said that the shift towards national currencies in trade among Commonwealth countries had helped them deal with Western sanctions. He also said a single currency for the bloc was not currently under consideration.
